title: Pope Leo XIV votes by mail in the US midterms
caption: The Vatican confirmed that Pope Leo XIV, born in Chicago, cast a mail-in ballot in Illinois ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections. He is the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election. Local officials said he requested the ballot on Oct. 3; how he voted is not known.

stories.name: Pope Leo XIV votes by mail in the US midterms
facts: The Holy See press office confirmed on Oct. 30 that Pope Leo XIV, born Robert Prevost in Chicago, cast a mail-in ballot in Illinois ahead of the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. He is the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election.
The Chicago Sun-Times first reported the vote, citing the Will County clerk's office, which said he requested the mail-in ballot on Oct. 3. He is registered at an address in New Lenox, Illinois.
The Vatican said he has voted whenever he was eligible, including while living in Peru. Who he voted for is not known.

artwork.alt: Graphic poster illustration: at sunset on a stone terrace beside the dome of St. Peter's Basilica, Pope Leo XIV in a white cassock and skullcap raises his arm after sending off a sealed airmail envelope. A dotted flight path arcs over the curve of the Atlantic to a small Chicago skyline, with the Willis Tower and Hancock Center, on the far horizon. It represents his mail-in vote in the U.S. midterms; the envelope is blank.
